hypothesis: H3 (variation practice): blocked practice looks better during acquisition but interleaved practice wins retention and transfer, because drilling one passage at a time lets each new passage overwrite the shared feature slots (motif and position onehots) that the other passages rely on (contextual interference; the Shea & Morgan 1979 crossover, in silico). Transfer specifically isolates the motif channel. Mechanism control: with passage-local features (no shared slots) the retention/transfer crossover should vanish and transfer should collapse to chance.

retention_last_blocked_gt_interleaved.note: just-drilled recency: DESIGN predicts blocked keeps the passage it drilled last — this is the anticipated mechanism, not a failed interleaving prediction

retention_earlier_interleaved_gt_blocked.note: the two earlier-drilled passages are where blocked's overwriting cost lives (order-relative form of the v1 per-passage secondaries)

nomotif_acquisition_gap.prediction: descriptive only (not verdict-gating): blocked's concentration advantage on currently-practiced material need not require shared slots

nomotif_retention_gap.prediction: no detectable gap by either test (raw p): without shared slots the interference that drives the retention half of the crossover is impossible

nomotif_transfer_gap.prediction: no detectable gap by either test (raw p), and both conditions at chance (1/8 within 0.05): the novel passage's local features are never trained

claims.name: acquisition
claims.claim: Blocked practice looks better during acquisition (greedy score on currently-practiced material) — the fool's-progress half of the crossover.
claims.evidence: blocked IQM 0.486 > interleaved 0.427; MW p=0.667 (Holm 1), Welch p=0.577 (Holm 1). Fragility disclosed at registration: the effect is small (~0.03 IQM) and alpha-marginal at n=40 (direction held in 13/13 fresh 40-seed verification batches of the v1 protocol; a fresh batch missed alpha).

claims.name: retention
claims.claim: Interleaved practice wins retention (mean greedy score on A, B, C after training).
claims.evidence: interleaved IQM 0.514 <= blocked 0.542; MW p=0.667 (Holm 1), Welch p=0.684 (Holm 1).

claims.name: transfer
claims.claim: Interleaved practice wins transfer to a novel passage built from the same motifs.
claims.evidence: interleaved IQM 0.375 > blocked 0.208; MW p=0.333 (Holm 1), Welch p=0.106 (Holm 0.317).

claims.name: mechanism
claims.claim: The retention/transfer crossover lives in the shared feature slots: with passage-local features (no shared slots) the gaps vanish and transfer collapses to chance.
claims.evidence: nomotif retention gap: blocked-nomotif IQM 0.503 vs interleaved-nomotif 0.475 (MW p=1, Welch p=0.697); nomotif transfer gap: 0.150 vs 0.125 (MW p=0.221, Welch p=0.205); chance = 0.125 +- 0.05.

conclusion.summary: Counterbalanced main pair — acquisition: blocked IQM 0.486 > interleaved 0.427 [boundary]; retention: interleaved IQM 0.514 <= blocked 0.542 [null]; transfer: interleaved IQM 0.375 > blocked 0.208 [boundary]. Mechanism control (no shared slots): [supported] — nomotif transfer IQMs 0.150/0.125 vs chance 0.125.

viz.story: Blocked drilling of one passage at a time rides the shared feature slots (motif and position onehots) to fast visible progress, then each new passage overwrites them; interleaving forces the shared weights to serve all passages at once — worse practice scores, better musician. The nomotif control pair repeats the protocol with passage-local features and no shared slots: the retention/transfer gaps should vanish and transfer collapse to chance, pinning the crossover on shared-parameter interference. Transfer isolates the motif channel specifically (the novel passage's own slots are never trained). Block order is counterbalanced across seeds (seed % 6), so retention is also reported relative to drill order (earlier vs last).
